newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CANTV workers aim for 12-hr work stoppage Monday.
newsitem.headline: CANTV workers aim for 12-hr work stoppage Monday.

text.p: Unions at Venezuelan telephone company CANTV said Thursday they would stage a nationwide 12-hour work stoppage Monday -- but company spokesmen said the walkout was illegal under Venezuelan labor laws.

"We've decided to walk out for 12 hours Monday," Cruz Hernandez, president of the umbrella telecommunications group Fetratel, told Reuters. "It is not illegal as we have sent a strike petition to the Labor Ministry," he said.
But Alexis Leoni, the company's director of institutional relations, told Reuters, "Legally, they can't strike."
Under Venezuelan labor law, strikes can only take place 120 hours after the decision to do so is taken, Leoni said, adding: "If they do strike, they'll be putting workers at risk".
Outside CANTV's headquarters in Caracas, hundreds of workers waved banners and cheered when the stoppage was announced.
But Leoni said only one hundred workers had attended the midday union meeting and that CANTV workers "felt more than ever they were part of the company".
On Wednesday, CANTV announced better-than-expected 1996 earnings of 208 billion bolivars ($436 million) -- nearly seven times 1995 profits.
CANTV workers have so far rejected outright four wage contract offers.

Company officials say the latest would have upped take home pay 37 percent in 1997 and 77 percent next year. But workers have said they want a 125 percent increase to compensate for triple-digit inflation last year and projected inflation of between 25 and 35 percent this year.
